subject: Agriculture
title: Multiple Origins of Farming
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Multiple Origins of Farming.

hook.text: Agriculture wasn't invented once. It emerged independently on at least seven continents and regions.

buildup.text: China domesticated rice and millet. Mesoamerica gave us corn, beans, and squash.

discovery.text: Africa developed sorghum and yams. South America domesticated potatoes and quinoa.

twist.text: These regions had no contact with each other. Farming was an idea whose time had come—everywhere.

climax.text: Climate change after the last Ice Age made farming possible. Warmer, stable weather opened the door.

punchline.text: The same idea, born independently, across the world.

quiz.question: How many independent origins of agriculture have been identified?
options: Just one, in the Fertile Crescent
At least seven, across different regions
